title: Testing That I Actually Run: A Small Pyramid

cover.alt: Concept illustration of a stable testing pyramid with a broad block foundation, a few integration pieces, and a small inspection lens.

figures.title: The testing stack used in this article
figures.summary: Keep the automated foundation focused and the release check manageable.

items.label: Pure logic
items.detail: Use Vitest for deterministic formatters, parsers, and permission checks.

items.label: Module boundaries
items.detail: Add a small number of integration tests with mocked network responses.

items.label: Release smoke check
items.detail: Manually check the main user flow, mobile menu, and links.

items.label: Continuous integration
items.detail: Run the fast automated suite away from the developer's laptop.

figures.caption: The author's approach for personal projects; it is not a universal replacement for end-to-end testing.

figures.title: From an edge case to a release check
figures.summary: Use repeatable checks where they provide practical confidence.

items.label: Implement
items.detail: Get the function working in a scratch file or REPL.

items.label: Test the boundary
items.detail: Cover meaningful null, empty, type, and exact-match cases.

items.label: Run locally
items.detail: Check the focused suite before committing.

items.label: Run in CI
items.detail: Repeat the automated checks after pushing.

items.label: Inspect the release
items.detail: Walk the smoke checklist in the target browsers.

figures.caption: The workflow described in the article. Manual and automated checks cover different risks.
